key_insight: An interpretable AI workflow for tissue-based neural autoantibody interpretation improved reader accuracy, especially for novice readers, compared with unaided interpretation.
clinical_relevance: This could make autoimmune encephalitis testing more consistent and reduce reader-dependent variability in specialized lab settings.
method: Trained on 2,357 retrospective serum and CSF tissue-based assay images from >80 institutions.
Validated prospectively on 200 images from 200 unique patients.
Compared expert and novice readers with and without AI assistance in a two-round blinded study.
evidence_signal: In prospective validation, the standalone classifier reached AUC 0.922 with 86.5% accuracy, while pooled reader accuracy rose from 90.4% unaided to 97.4% with AI assistance.
watch_item: Results were generated in a centralized-lab setting, so cross-platform and multicentre generalizability still needs confirmation.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study
